correctness.rationale: For each b, squaring the Fourier sum and restricting to the polar kernel yields exactly N^d r_b or zero; character extension counts N^d/r_b nonzero a. Fourier inversion yields the endpoint norm and translation averaging proves minimality among all projections. Integral Smith diagonalization determines every kernel size. A direct two-generator cokernel recurrence determines the three cycle types, and the resulting dyadic sums and constants are checked symbolically. Exact integer cyclotomic exhaustive tests cover cycle pairs (3,1),(3,2),(3,3),(4,1),(4,2),(5,1),(6,1),(8,1), plus unrelated quadratic forms at N=2,3,4,5. All-dimensional claims rest on proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The sharp endpoint norm is the smallest attainable stability constant among all projections onto a canonical finite quadratic Fourier subspace; the theorem makes it a Smith-invariant quantity and determines its entire magnitude distribution. Its explicit cycle family has a full-power modulus exponent drop exactly when the adjacency polar matrix acquires a two-dimensional integer nullspace (n divisible by four). This is a motivated infinite family classification and a reusable structural norm law, not an arbitrary finite census.
